Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — indemnity scope (Skyward Bio)

Elaine,

Thanks — got the redlines and attached doc. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Marissa (contracts) to take a look. High level thoughts below:
- We typically carve out claims that arise solely from Customer-supplied content (e.g., the customer uploads a copyrighted file) and from public-domain prompts; model-output-only infringement claims are more complex and we prefer to manage/defend with cooperation rather than a blanket transfer.
- A 10-day notice window is tight for patent/takedown investigations. We can be flexible but will need at least 30 days to investigate and coordinate defense or remediation.
- Material increases to the insurance requirement will affect pricing / discounting and could trigger approval for additional commercial terms.

Kimberly, can you propose fallback language? My suggested middle ground: limited defend obligation for third-party copyright/patent claims tied to (i) prompt attribution (if claim relates to specific customer prompt/output), (ii) a minimum evidence threshold, and (iii) an option for us to transfer defense for software-specific patents at customer cost.

I'm available Wed 11:00-12:30 PT or Thu 14:00 PT if a call helps.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order Form redlines — indemnity scope (Skyward Bio)

Team — I reviewed Skyward's redlines (attached redwood_response_redlines.docx) and drafted a response we can push on this deal. Summary of our proposed positions:

1) Scope carveouts:
- We will agree to a carveout for Customer Data and Customer-supplied code (i.e., we will not accept indemnity for claims arising solely from content the customer uploaded/owned).
- We will NOT accept a blanket carveout for "model output" unless tied to specific evidence that the output reproduces a protected work verbatim.

2) Defense vs. Reimburse:
- Offer a hybrid: Redwood will defend (control counsel selection and settlement) for third-party copyright claims where the evidence shows verbatim reproduction or code copy; for broad allegations or patent assertions related to customer prompts, we propose a reimbursement model (Redwood will work with Customer to investigate; Customer may elect to take over defense at its own cost).

3) Notice and cooperation:
- Counter-propose 30 days' notice for written claim notice, with a requirement that the claimant provide a reasonably detailed claim package (claim letter, evidence, sample outputs).

4) Insurance and caps: 
- We are willing to accept a one-time increase in the insurance requirement for this named account for the duration of the contract, but any change must be tied to a commercial uplift (we should mark this in the deal). Also keep our standard liability cap (per order form) intact; do not agree to uncapped liability.

5) Subrogation and indemnity transfer:
- Allow subrogation but exclude our indemnity for third-party claims that arise from the Customer's breach of the Acceptable Use Policy or from their modifications to the model or outputs.

I have inline edits and proposed redline language in the attached docx. If the commercial team agrees to attach a small uplift (we've historically taken 5-12% list price lift for higher insurance), I think we can close this with a moderate compromise.

Next steps: Marissa, please confirm pricing impact. Priyom, please propose the call time you offered and I will join. Elaine, if your legal team can accept the hybrid defense/reimburse structure and the 30-day notice, that should move things forward.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
